subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose a cross-channel Gateway receipt timestamp to agents, and if so what stable field name, trust block, and timestamp format should it use?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix creates durable agent-visible prompt metadata and likely plugin SDK/channel ingress surface, so automation should not choose the public contract unilaterally.

options.title: Add generic receipt timestamp
options.body: Expose a single field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` through the chosen metadata block and carry it through the generic SDK/channel ingress path with cross-channel tests.

options.title: Keep timing in diagnostics only
options.body: Do not add agent-visible metadata; instead solve attribution through Gateway/channel trace events or logs.

options.title: Leave timing to plugins
options.body: Allow each channel plugin to expose its own receipt timing, accepting weaker cross-channel consistency.

recommendation.title: Add generic receipt timestamp
recommendation.body: Expose a single field such as `gatewayReceivedAt` through the chosen metadata block and carry it through the generic SDK/channel ingress path with cross-channel tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current routing candidate for the prompt metadata and plugin SDK boundary decision.
